plain_description.what: The full 12-model match schedule (9,123 matches with a reference, 18,246 calls) was re-judged through the actual production Kotlin code path with the shipped judge, and compared with the earlier Python-judged results.
plain_description.why: An earlier smaller check had failed to match the two paths, so the production pipeline had no board of record of its own.
plain_description.information: Agreement shows the shipped code behaves like the research code, so production rankings can be trusted. Divergence would mean a wiring problem. Result: done, descriptive. On the large set the two paths agree within the judge's own noise (+0.4 / +0.2 points), so the earlier failure was a small-sample effect, and this run is now the production board of record. A side finding: one statistical parameter of the confidence formula was identified on one draw of the same judge on the same data but not on another, so it is fragile on a single draw. Pooling both draws reaches the registered bar but not a stricter honest test (p about 0.07). Later ruled history rather than evidence, because it ran on the older question pool.
